RebelMyForms.ColumnAvgFieldTimeDocumentation: The average time a visitor had the field in focus. A long time points at a field that is hard to answer.
RebelMyForms.ColumnAvgFormTimeDocumentation: The average time from the first field a visitor used to the last one, or to the submit.
RebelMyForms.ColumnAvgHesitationDocumentation: The average time a visitor had the focus in the field before they first typed or chose something. A long hesitation points at a question that is unclear.
RebelMyForms.ColumnAvgWaitDocumentation: The average time from when the form was on the page until a visitor first used it. A long time can mean that the form is far down the page or that visitors read before they start.
RebelMyForms.ColumnBlankDocumentation: How often the field was empty when the form was submitted.
RebelMyForms.ColumnChangesDocumentation: How often the content of the field was changed. Many more changes than visitors who used the field means they corrected their answer.
RebelMyForms.ColumnDropoffRateDocumentation: The share of the visitors who used the field for whom it was the last one before they left without submitting.
RebelMyForms.ColumnDropoffsDocumentation: How often the field was the last one a visitor used before they left without submitting the form.
RebelMyForms.ColumnInteractionsDocumentation: How often the field was used: a visitor put the focus in it or changed it.
RebelMyForms.ColumnInvalidDocumentation: How often the browser refused to send the form because of this field: it was required and empty, or what was typed did not fit its type or pattern.
RebelMyForms.ColumnPositionDocumentation: The place of the field in the form, counted from the top. The fields are listed in this order, so the drop-offs read from the start of the form to its end.
RebelMyForms.ColumnRefocusesDocumentation: How often a visitor came back to the field after leaving it.
RebelMyForms.ColumnResubmitsDocumentation: How often the form was submitted more than once in the same page view. That usually means the website refused the first attempt.
RebelMyForms.ColumnStartRateDocumentation: The share of the times the form was seen that a visitor started to fill it in.
RebelMyForms.ColumnStartsDocumentation: How often a visitor started to fill in the form: they used at least one field.
RebelMyForms.ColumnSubmissionsDocumentation: How often the form was submitted.
RebelMyForms.ColumnSubmitRateDocumentation: The share of the started forms that were submitted.
RebelMyForms.ColumnSuccessesDocumentation: How often the website said the form went through. It is counted for a website that calls RebelMyForms.success().
RebelMyForms.ColumnViewsDocumentation: How often a page with the form was loaded. A form counts once for each page view.
RebelMyForms.DocApi: The reports are available in the reporting API of Matomo, for users with view access to the website:
RebelMyForms.DocContainers: An element with the attribute data-rebel-form is tracked as a form, with the fields inside it. As nothing is submitted by the browser, call RebelMyForms.success() when it is done.
RebelMyForms.DocContainersTitle: Forms that are not a form element
RebelMyForms.DocFields: Click a form to see its fields. "Used by" is how often a visitor put the focus in the field or changed it. A long time in a field points at a question that is hard to answer. Many more changes than uses mean that visitors correct their answer. "Returns" is how often a visitor came back to the field. "Left empty" is how often the field was empty when the form was submitted, and "Refused by browser" how often the browser would not send the form because of the field. "Drop-offs" is how often the field was the last one of a visitor who left without submitting: the field where they gave up. "Avg. hesitation" is how long a visitor had the focus in the field before they first answered it. On a form, "Avg. time to start" is how long the form was on the page before a visitor first used it.
RebelMyForms.DocForms: Every form element on a page, up to %1$s forms on a page and %2$s fields in a form. A form that is added after the page was loaded is counted when a visitor first uses it. Hidden fields and buttons are not fields.
RebelMyForms.DocIgnore: Add the attribute data-rebel-ignore to a form or a field that is not to be tracked. To stop tracking all forms of a website, turn off "Track forms" under Administration > Websites > Manage.
RebelMyForms.DocIgnoreTitle: Leaving a form or a field out
RebelMyForms.DocIntro: Rebel My Forms shows how the visitors of a website use its forms: how often each form is seen, started and submitted, and what happens in each field. What visitors type is never collected. Only the names of forms and fields, times and counts are sent.
RebelMyForms.DocNames: A form is named by the first of these that it has: the attribute data-rebel-form, its id, its name, the path of its action. A field is named by data-rebel-field, its name, its id or its type. Give a form a name of your own when the same form has different IDs on different pages:
RebelMyForms.DocNamesTitle: The names of forms and fields
RebelMyForms.DocReports: Forms in the reporting menu shows the chosen website and period. "Forms over time" is a graph of the form views, starts, submissions, the start rate or the submit rate, and "Forms in numbers" gives the same for the period. "Forms" lists each form. A form is seen once for each page view it is on, and started when a visitor uses one of its fields. The start rate is the share of the views that were started, and the submit rate the share of the starts that were submitted. "Forms by page" shows the pages the forms are on. The visit log lists the forms a visitor started. "Forms by device type" shows how the forms do on each kind of device. "Fields of all forms" lists every field of every form, and is where a field can be followed over time with row evolution.
RebelMyForms.DocSegments: The segment "Form" narrows any report of Matomo to the visits that saw a form, and "Form outcome" to the visits that got so far with a form: seen, abandoned (started and not submitted), submitted or succeeded. Use them to compare the visitors who gave up with the ones who submitted, by device or by where they came from. A segment works on visits: on the Forms page it shows all forms of the visits that match. Some segments to start from:
RebelMyForms.DocStart: Nothing has to change in the tracking code of a website. The plugin adds itself to the JavaScript tracker of Matomo, also when the tracker is loaded through Matomo Tag Manager. If Matomo is not allowed to write the tracker file, an administrator of the server runs this once after the plugin is activated or updated:
RebelMyForms.DocStored: A form is sent when the page is loaded, and again when it is submitted or the visitor leaves. A visit stores at most %s forms. The address of the page is stored without what follows ? and #. Forms go through the tracker of Matomo, so consent, opt-out and the exclusions of the website apply, and they are deleted together with the visit they belong to. A form is not a page view and does not change the other reports.
RebelMyForms.DocSubmitted: A form counts as submitted when the browser sends it, also when the website then refuses what was sent. "Submitted again" counts the forms that were submitted more than once in the same page view, which usually means the website refused the first attempt.
RebelMyForms.DocSuccess: The browser cannot know whether the website accepted a form. Let the website say so, with the form element when the page stays, or with the name of the form on the page that follows. The form then counts as "Went through". The same call marks a form as submitted when it is not sent by the browser, as in a single-page application.
RebelMyForms.DocSuccessTitle: Telling when a form went through
RebelMyForms.FieldsDocumentation: The fields of the form: how visitors used each of them, and which field they were in when they gave up.
RebelMyForms.FieldsOfAllFormsDocumentation: Every field of every form, named by its form and its own name, with the fields where most visitors gave up first. Use row evolution here to follow a field over time, for example after a form was changed.
RebelMyForms.FormsByDeviceDocumentation: How the forms do on each kind of device. A form that is started less or submitted less on smartphones is often hard to use on a small screen.
RebelMyForms.FormsByPageDocumentation: The pages the forms are on, without what follows ? and # in their address, with how often a form on the page was seen, started and submitted.
RebelMyForms.FormsOverTimeDocumentation: How often the forms of the website were seen, started and submitted.
RebelMyForms.FormsReportDocumentation: The forms of the website: how often each was seen, started and submitted, and how long visitors spent in it. Click a form to see its fields. What visitors type is never collected.
RebelMyForms.PluginDescription: See how visitors use the forms on your website: who starts, who submits, and which fields make them hesitate or leave.
RebelMyForms.SettingEnabledHelp: Store how the visitors of this website use its forms.
